issue.title: Pronouns stated as a fact instead of just used
issue.symptom:
Found 2026-11-12 in GAIA's Grotto: asked "do you remember Nick?", she replied "I do -- Azrael's friend. His name's Nick and his pronouns are he/him." The "pronouns are X/Y" clause is unprompted bookkeeping leaking into conversation -- pronoun usage should just show through word choice, not be announced.

Root cause: gaia_common/utils/people.py's pronoun_words() phrases the in-prompt instruction as a FACT ("X's pronouns are Y; use them when you speak of X"), which the model treats as content worth relaying rather than a silent style note. Fixed by rephrasing as a direct writing instruction ("When you write about X, use Y -- just use it, don't mention it"), matching the house style already used right next to it in speaker_line ("Speak to them as 'you', never in the third person"). Azrael's framing: the pronoun should be obvious from usage alone, no need to ever say "pronouns are X/Y" unless directly asked.

Updated all affected call sites' tests (test_people_751u.py -- added direct pronoun_words coverage, none existed before; test_conversation_memory.py -- 5 existing assertions checking the old fact-shaped phrase). 1632 gaia-core + 1034 gaia-common tests pass, ruff clean, mypy clean.

investigation.format: issue_investigation actions: SEARCH / READ / PLACE + NOTE

gold_steps.action: SEARCH: , never in the third person
gold_steps.why: a phrase or name from the issue, as it appears in code
gold_steps.result_line: gaia-common/gaia_common/utils/people.py:234: line += ". Speak to them as \"you\", never in the third person. " + pronoun_words(person) + "."

gold_steps.note: Asked "do you remember Nick?" she replied "His name's Nick and his pronouns are he/him" -- nobody asked. The in-prompt instruction told her "X's pronouns are Y; use them when you speak of X" -- fact-shaped text that reads as content worth relaying, not a silent style note.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/tests/test_people_751u.py
"""People (751u): she knows who she's speaking with."""

from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from gaia_common.utils.people import PeopleRegistry, claimed_name, pronoun_words, speaker_line

AZRAEL_ID = "596925786208993283"
DM = f"discord_dm_{AZRAEL_ID}"
WEB = "web_3132edcd"


@pytest.fixture


def test_pronoun_words_is_a_writing_instruction_not_a_fact(people):
    # Found 2026-11-12, GAIA's Grotto: phrased as "X's pronouns are Y; use
    # them", she echoed it back unprompted ("his pronouns are he/him"). It
    # must never again read as something there is content to relay.
    nick = people.create("Nick", [{"kind": "session", "id": WEB}])
    people.set_pronouns(nick["id"], "he/him", source="said so")
    line = pronoun_words(people.get(nick["id"]))
    assert line == 'When you write about Nick, use "he/him" — just use it, don\'t mention it'
    assert "pronouns are" not in line  # the exact fact-shaped phrase that got echoed back

    unknown = people.create("Priya", [{"kind": "session", "id": "web_9"}])
    line = pronoun_words(people.get(unknown["id"]))
    assert "Priya" in line and "they" in line and "not something to bring up" in line
    assert "Priya's pronouns" not in line  # the fact-shaped phrase, not "no pronouns are on record"
